title: Hermes
subtitle: hermes-agent (OSS) + Langfuse + HITL
description: Nous Research's hermes-agent is the open-source harness (MIT-licensed) — what's here is what I built around it: a nightly Langfuse eval loop and a weekly self-improvement cron that clusters its own low-quality turns and proposes fixes to its own prompt, running on a 3-node homelab with a hand-patched local inference layer. One real run: 11 low-quality turns, 3 proposed fixes, 2 applied, 1 correctly rejected as wrong for the context — nothing changes without my approval.

title: Pi-Cloud
subtitle: High-Performance Edge Gateway
description: A high-performance private cloud orchestrating 10 microservices on a Raspberry Pi 5. This setup replaces Big Tech ecosystems for photo storage and identity management with a zero-trust, invisible infrastructure. It features a recursive Unbound + Pi-hole DNS stack for low-latency ad-filtering, atomic disaster recovery, and a unified 'Single Pane of Glass' telemetry dashboard.

title: Inference Engine
subtitle: llama.cpp + ROCm + Local Agentic Workflows
description: The engine behind every local agentic workflow I run — reachable from my phone over Telegram, with every call traced and nightly graded by its own eval loop. A hand-patched llama.cpp build on GPU hardware the project doesn't officially support, tuned through a memory-allocator bug and a week-long regression that fooled every obvious diagnosis before the real bug turned up somewhere nobody expected to find it.

title: AI Chat Assistant
subtitle: Gemini 2.5 Flash + Cloudflare Workers + Keyword RAG
description: The assistant in the corner of this page — ask it about any project and it'll actually know. Deliberately built on keyword-scored retrieval instead of vector search: no embedding service, fully deterministic, and free to run (Cloudflare's 100K req/day plus Gemini's free tier add up to $0/month). Structured output from the model drives real UI — action buttons that open a resume or jump to a section, not just more text.

title: myPal
subtitle: Rapid Prototyping Case Study for Assistive Tech
description: An AAC (Augmentative and Alternative Communication) tool designed for rapid deployment in low-resource environments. Architected with an offline-first SQLite schema for reliable data persistence without network dependency, paired with React Native cross-platform synchronization to enable seamless iOS/Android parity. Focused on assistive tech accessibility for children with autism and speech delays, demonstrating how technical constraints (limited connectivity, diverse devices) can drive scalable architectural decisions.
